transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-06 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO, Verdant), Tom Rivera (DevOps Lead), Lena Park (Security Engineer), Marta Ruiz (Compliance), Evan Cho (SRE)

--- Optional auto sections may be incomplete ---
Summary: posture review focused on SOC2, KMS, SSO/RBAC and incident escalation + tabletop.

00:00 - Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro — jordan from redwood, priya is our platform se, we'll run through the posture and then propose a tabletop.
00:18 - Aisha: thanks, yeah we wanted to validate the incident flow and make sure keys and logs meet our EU residency / audit reqs.
00:32 - Priya: great, real quick agenda: soc2 docs, sso/rbac, audit log retention, kms options (customer-managed vs redwood-managed), incident tiers and runbook, and then proposed drill. sound ok?
00:45 - Tom: sounds good. also want to understand RTO/RPO expectations for both hosted api and dedicated pools.
01:05 - Jordan: noted. first, soc2 — we maintain a SOC 2 Type II; we can share the attestation and an executive summary. that covers control tests, change management, etc.
01:22 - Marta: will want the report and the scope. do you include private deployments in the scope?
01:34 - Priya: yes, for private we have an enterprise package where the control environment expands — we include access controls and deployment audits. full SOC scope doc will be attached.
01:50 - Lena: on pentest, do you run external third party tests and can we see the remediation timeline?
02:03 - Jordan: we do annual pen tests and internal devsecops scans. we can share redacted report and remediation notes.
02:18 - Aisha: good. next — sso and rbac. we use SAML IdP with SCIM provisioning. can we map groups to role policies?
02:34 - Priya: yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM. roles map to token scopes and you can do route-level restrictions. small caveat: some internal tooling mis-tags service tokens occasionally — there's an audit path to fix but it's rare.
02:57 - Evan: is there per-token owner metadata in the logs?
03:10 - Priya: logs include token id, issuing principal, route, model, and region. retention default is 90 days for hosted, configurable for dedicated/private.
03:28 - Tom: retention longer than a year sometimes necessary for compliance, do you support archival to customer S3 in-region?
03:42 - Jordan: yes we have an option to ship logs to a customer S3 or syslog endpoint in the same region. we also support longer retention in enterprise tiers.
03:55 - Marta: for EU data residency we need keys and logs to remain in eu-central. how do you guarantee key residency?
04:10 - Priya: for customer-managed keys you bring your own KMS (we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM solutions via KMIP). keys never leave the region unless you choose cross-region replication. for redwood-managed keys we can pin the key to a region but it's still in our control plane — for the strictest residency customers we recommend customer-managed KMS with HSM.
04:37 - Lena: technical nicety: how do you handle token encryption in transit vs at rest?
04:45 - Priya: all traffic uses TLS 1.2+ with mutual TLS for private deployments if configured. at-rest encryption uses AES-256 and keys are in KMS. KV cache is encrypted and rotated per customer policy.
05:05 - Aisha: talk through incident tiers — what's 1 vs 2 vs 3, and how does paging/escalation work?
05:18 - Jordan: we typically have Tier 1 (degraded performance), Tier 2 (partial outage or degradation of a critical region), Tier 3 (full service outage affecting SLAs). escalation: on-call SRE -> SE/AE escalation -> engineering incident manager -> executive notification.
05:35 - Evan: do you support customer-triggered failover to another region and what's the expected RTO?
05:44 - Priya: for hosted tier, automated fallback to a compatible model in another region is possible but depends on model variants and warm cache. typical RTO measured in minutes for routing but RPO depends on KV cache and prefix caching — if you need near-zero RPO we recommend Dedicated with cross-region replication for KV and synchronous backups.
06:12 - Tom: give ballpark numbers for Dedicated: what's the RTO and RPO you can promise?
06:20 - Priya: for Dedicated with warm standby and replicated state we have seen RTO ~5-15 minutes for routing + container spin up, RPO ~0-2 minutes if you enable synchronous replication; without replication RPO could be tens of minutes. these are dependent on session lengths and how much KV you persist.
06:48 - Marta: what about uptime SLA?
06:52 - Jordan: standard hosted SLA is 99.9%. Dedicated SLA can be 99.95% with reserved pools and redundancy. enterprise agreements can negotiate higher windows.
07:05 - Aisha: what's your error budget and do you provide credits?
07:12 - Jordan: yes, credits tied to monthly availability. we'll share our SLA terms in the agreement.
07:22 - Lena: for escalation, can Verdant have a dedicated incident liaison at Redwood for high-tier incidents?
07:30 - Jordan: for enterprise contracts we offer a named escalation contact and a PagerDuty integration.
07:38 - Evan: show us the incident runbook briefly.
07:44 - Priya: (screen share described) — step 1 detect and annotate incident in infra tooling, step 2 assemble SRE + SE, step 3 determine containment strategy (route to fallback, ramp up dedicated pool), step 4 notify customer via configured channel, step 5 postmortem and RCA within sla window.
08:12 - Tom: what channels for notifications — email, webhooks, slack, pagerduty?
08:20 - Priya: all of the above. customers can pick primary and secondary.
08:28 - Aisha: for the tabletop, we want to simulate a KV cache corruption in EU region. what do you recommend as the play sequence?
08:40 - Priya: recommended: (a) declare incident, (b) run isolation to prevent read/writes from corrupting further, (c) switch traffic to warm standby region with compatible model, (d) restore KV from replica or snapshot, (e) validate, (f) failback. we'll hold a dry run to time each step.
09:05 - Jordan: important to capture RTO and RPO during the drill; we'll instrument metrics.
09:12 - Lena: how do you prove the KMS integration was correct after failover? i.e., keys didn't leak or get re-wrapped incorrectly.
09:22 - Priya: audit chain: key usage logs, key wrapping logs, and KMS access logs. if using customer KMS we don't see raw keys; we only see key ids used. we'll provide the key usage report as part of the postmortem.
09:40 - Evan: are audit logs immutable? can we append-only them in an archive?
09:47 - Jordan: we support write-once archival to customer S3 with object lock if required, and also send logs to SIEM in append-only mode.
09:58 - Marta: retention and encryption — we need logs retained 7 years for a subset. is that supported?
10:08 - Priya: yes, with custom retention and archival policies. long term retention is an enterprise feature; costs apply.
10:20 - Tom: ok for proof — can you share a redacted incident postmortem as an example?
10:27 - Jordan: yes, will attach a redacted pm and the sla credits template.
10:33 - Aisha: how about breach notification windows? we have legal obligations.
10:40 - Priya: we support 72-hour initial notification SLA for confirmed breaches, and we align with the customer on contact lists and legal escalation. that will be codified in the contract.
11:00 - Evan: are there runbook playbooks for degraded latency (hot loops) vs full outage?
11:08 - Priya: yes, different playbooks: degrade -> throttle/burst limit and route to fallback; outage -> failover and capacity spinup. we'll share the playbook library.
11:28 - Tom: on the KMS front — do you support rotating keys without downtime?
11:35 - Priya: yes, key rotation is online if you use envelope encryption: rotate data-encrypting-keys while master keys rewrap. with customer-managed KMS that's seamless as long as the KMS supports rewrap APIs.
11:50 - Lena: want to confirm RBAC granularity: can we restrict model types per team and restrict embeddings export?
11:58 - Priya: yes, role policies can be per-model and per-route and you can restrict export or snapshot operations to certain roles. enforcement is at token validation time.
12:15 - Jordan: ok wrapping toward tabletop — propose we do the EU KV corruption sim: Verdant will provide pre-defined dataset and runbook lane, Redwood will time each step and instrument metrics. proposal: 60-min drill, followed by 30-min debrief next day.
12:34 - Aisha: agreed in principle; Marta will confirm compliance attendees and Evan will prepare SRE steps.
12:42 - Jordan: next steps recap: i will send SOC2 & pen test artifacts, priya will send KMS integration checklist, we schedule the drill week of Oct 20.
12:55 - Tom: one last Q — if we want customer-managed HSM with KMIP, is there an extra engineering integration fee?
13:06 - Jordan: usually a one-time integration engineering fee for initial onboarding; will put a range in the quote.
13:16 - Marta: ok that works.
13:22 - Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.
13:30 - Aisha: thanks, bye.

--- End transcript ---
